articles.body: A current-state projection removes a merchant record. Later, an older update for that key arrives and the record comes back. The delete worked. The consumer forgot enough ordering information to accept stale state afterward. Here is a small Python experiment that separates the visible value from the latest version applied to its key. The source order and delivery order differ Assume a single source namespace and a strictly ordered integer version per key. Higher versions describe newer source state. Payloads at a given version are immutable. Source version Operation Value 1 upsert merchant-7 10 2 upsert merchant-7 20 3 delete merchant-7 absent Now deliver versions in the order 1, 3, 2.

articles.title: Address poisoning: the copy-paste habit that cost one trader 49,999,950 USDT
articles.excerpt: By send21 Many crypto theft stories involve a hacked exchange or a leaked seed phrase. Address poisoning needs neither. No key is stolen and no code is exploited. The victim signs a perfectly valid tr…
articles.body: By send21 Many crypto theft stories involve a hacked exchange or a leaked seed phrase. Address poisoning needs neither. No key is stolen and no code is exploited. The victim signs a perfectly valid transaction from their own wallet, to an address they chose themselves. It just happens to be the wrong address. This post explains how the attack works, what the research says about its scale, and the habits that make it much harder to fall for. How the attack works On chains like Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain, an address is a 40-character hexadecimal string. Nobody memorizes those. So, as a peer-reviewed USENIX Security 2025 paper titled "Blockchain Address Poisoning" puts it, users often select addresses from their recent transaction history. That habit is the whole attack surface.
articles.author: send21

articles.title: I blamed fillets for my STL-to-CAD failures. The original STEP files said otherwise
articles.excerpt: mesh2cad turns an STL back into CAD: a STEP file with real planes, cylinders and cones, plus a CadQuery or OpenSCAD script when the part is simple enough. I test it on six real Original Prusa i3 MK3S…
articles.body: mesh2cad turns an STL back into CAD: a STEP file with real planes, cylinders and cones, plus a CadQuery or OpenSCAD script when the part is simple enough. I test it on six real Original Prusa i3 MK3S printer parts, because synthetic test shapes lied to me before . After 0.10.0, two of the six came back as exact STEP solids. The other four fell back to a faceted solid (valid, but just triangles glued into faces). The tool reported a small "unfitted" area on each, and I wrote in the README that these were probably edge rounds: torus fillets and sphere corners that the fitter didn't know yet. That was wrong, and finding out how it was wrong is what made 0.11.0 work.

articles.title: Day 22: Autonomous Agents — From Passive LLMs to Goal-Driven Execution
articles.excerpt: Early generative AI was passive: you send a prompt, the model returns text, and a human decides what to do next. That is useful for drafting, but it cannot run a business workflow on its own. The next…
articles.body: Early generative AI was passive : you send a prompt, the model returns text, and a human decides what to do next. That is useful for drafting, but it cannot run a business workflow on its own. The next step is the autonomous agent : a system that can plan, check its own progress and carry out a multi-step goal with little human intervention. In plain terms: A chatbot is a colleague who answers your question and then waits. An agent is a colleague you give a task to, who comes back when it is done, or when they are stuck. Diagram: A passive LLM returns one text answer and a human decides the next step. An autonomous agent takes a goal and plans, acts, checks the result and repeats with little human intervention. That makes it useful for workflows and also riskier, so guardrails matter.

articles.title: Van Gogh's 'The Starry Night' depicts the sky on July 22, 1889, researchers find
articles.excerpt: Researchers think they might have pinpointed the exact night sky that we see depicted in Vincent van Gogh's iconic painting "The Starry Night."
articles.body: Researchers think they might have pinpointed the exact night sky that we see depicted in Vincent van Gogh's iconic painting "The Starry Night." Perhaps one of the most famous paintings in modern history, Van Gogh's "The Starry Night" carries a legacy that continues to inspire and mystify generation after generation. But while you might see in its swirls of color and bright spots of starlight a night sky derived purely from imagination, some scientists think it represents an actual view — one that includes a waning crescent moon, Venus and the Hyades cluster. And they may know exactly when this sky appeared.. In a new study, researchers suggest that "The Starry Night" depicts the pre-dawn sky seen around July 22, 1889 from Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, where Van Gogh painted it.

articles.title: Australia's bizarre 'Spider Crater' seen from orbit | Space photo of the day for Oct. 22, 2026
articles.excerpt: A satellite image of "Spider Crater" in Western Australia.
articles.body: A satellite image of "Spider Crater" in Western Australia. (Image credit: NASA Earth Observatory image by Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey ) From the dangerous Sydney funnel-web to the common huntsman, Australia is home to its fair share of spiders. It even has a crater shaped like one. What is it? One stretch of the vast Western Australia wilderness is imprinted with a curious crater, which likely formed after a meteor impact hundreds of millions of years ago. Geologists think the spider-like pattern in the crater's center was created when its floor rebounded following the initial impact, NASA has said . In the hundreds of millions of years since the initial impact, erosion has continued to carve this formation into its current, signature shape.

articles.title: Next Mass Effect game cancelled as EA shuts down legendary sci-fi RPG studio BioWare
articles.excerpt: The legendary RPG studio behind classics such as Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Mass Effect, and Dragon Age is no more.
articles.body: The writing was on the wall, but the news still hit us like a truck yesterday. BioWare, the iconic RPG studio behind the Mass Effect and Dragon Age series, is no more. Development on the next Mass Effect has stopped, but EA might not be entirely done with the IP. Variety reported, backed by EA’s own statement and BioWare’s goodbye on socials , that EA is laying off 3% of its global workforce and closing down BioWare. The shift comes shortly after the company went fully private this summer , with Saudi Arabia and private equity acquiring it alongside all its studios and properties.
